text: {"distance_m": 2.5, "reasoning_short": "Estimate only, from typical threshold data: the spot is a low-contrast detection target, not a resolution target, so 20/20 acuity alone doesn't set the limit. For tiny spots, area times threshold contrast is roughly constant (Ricco's law). Remembered photopic detection data (Blackwell-type, ~50–100 cd/m² indoor skin) put a 1 arcmin spot's threshold near 50% contrast. At 30% contrast the spot must subtend about 1.3 arcmin (~3.8e-4 rad). A 1 mm spot reaches that at 1 mm / 3.8e-4 ≈ 2.6 m, so about 2.5 m (plausibly 2–3 m)."}
